Question B-003-012-007.

Why the correct answer is right: Overmodulation drives SSB beyond its clean range; the audio distorts and the occupied bandwidth grows.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "It becomes distorted and occupies more bandwidth": This is the correct choice because overmodulation drives SSB beyond its clean range; the audio distorts and the occupied bandwidth grows.
- sourceIndex 1: "It increases the range of your signal": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from It becomes distorted and occupies more bandwidth. In SSB microphone level, carrier suppression, sideband frequency, and peak envelope power, more of that quantity would not address the fault and can make a clean-signal problem worse.
- sourceIndex 2: "It occupies less bandwidth and has a poor high frequency response": This answer would fit a different fault than It becomes distorted and occupies more bandwidth. In SSB microphone level, carrier suppression, sideband frequency, and peak envelope power, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 3: "It has higher fidelity and an improved signal-to-noise ratio": This option confuses another station topic with It becomes distorted and occupies more bandwidth. In SSB microphone level, carrier suppression, sideband frequency, and peak envelope power, more of that quantity would not address the fault and can make a clean-signal problem worse.
